data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A decentralized network is LESS resilient to correlated failure than a highly redundant monolith when the 'shared cause' is a dependency on a common substrate (e.g., a single DNS provider, cloud region, or OS kernel vulnerability).","counterconditions":[{"case":"The decentralized services use fundamentally different infrastructure providers.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The monolith's internal redundancy is implemented across heterogeneous hardware/software stacks.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The 'Substrate Convergence' effect: while services are independently operated, they converge on a small set of optimized, third-party infrastructure tools to remain viable, creating a hidden monolithic failure point that bypasses internal redundancy.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
